text: The fourth season of RuPaul's Drag Race began airing on January 30, 2012, and concluded on April 30, 2012. The cast was announced on November 13, 2011. The winner of the season was Sharon Needles, with Chad Michaels and Phi Phi O'Hara as runners-up, marking the first time in the show's history that two runners-up were named. The final featured a three-way lip-sync battle instead of the usual two, and the winner was not crowned in the studio but during the "Reunited" episode, which was filmed in front of a live audience. This was also the first season in which three versions of the finale were filmed, with each Top 3 contestant being crowned to prevent spoilers, following the leak of Raja's Season 3 win by Perez Hilton in 2011. Santino Rice and Billy B (Billy Brasfield), a celebrity makeup artist and star of the HGTV mini-series Hometown Renovation, shared the judges' seat alternately, with Brasfield filling in for Rice when needed, and both appeared side-by-side in the audience during the "Reunited" episode. The theme song played during the runway every episode was "Glamazon," and the song played during the credits was "The Beginning," both from RuPaul's album Glamazon. This season marked the first time a contestant, Willam Belli, was disqualified for breaking the rules, and the second consecutive season in which a contestant, Kenya Michaels, was brought back after being eliminated earlier. Jiggly Caliente, who placed 8th, later served as a judge on Drag Race Philippines and died on April 27, 2025. The premiere episode averaged a 0.6 rating in the 18-49 demographic, totaling 481,000 viewers, making it the highest-rated premiere in Logo's network history, while the finale scored a 0.7 rating and drew 601,000 viewers, with the "Reunited" episode becoming the highest-rated episode of the season and the highest-rated reunion in the franchise's history, seeing a 33% increase in the 18-49 demographic compared to Season 3. The season finale also registered five trending topics on Twitter, including Sharon Needles, Phi Phi, Willam, and the portmanteau "RuPaulogize," and ranked 4th among non-sports cable programs on Trendrr. During the season, the show's Twitter following increased by 77% and the Facebook page saw a 36% increase in likes. Logo released the second running of Fantasy Drag Race, an online fan contest inspired by fantasy football, where viewers assembled a team of three season four contestants, earning points based on performance and completing tasks, with the highest scorers receiving Drag Race and NYX Cosmetics products and one player winning a trip for two to the first stop on Logo's Drag Race Tour. The season also saw increased engagement on social media platforms, with Logo expanding its presence on Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, GetGlue, and Foursquare, hosting live tweets from RuPaul and contestants, and LogoTalk! chat parties. Season four specifically increased its focus on Tumblr, publishing animated GIFs, contestant trading cards, and internet meme-based images. TV.com named it the best reality show on television. In January 2012, the premiere episode generated eight US trending topics on Twitter and reached a 7th place ranking on Trendrr, and the show's Facebook page saw an 89% increase in followers, earning over half a million fans. At the end of the season, RuPaul revealed that Kenya Michaels had been voted back into the competition, and Latrice Royale was named Miss Congeniality. The final challenge involved the queens starring in RuPaul's music video "Glamazon" and acting in a dramatic scene with RuPaul. All three finalists lip-synced to "Glamazon" during the runway, and RuPaul announced that the winner would be revealed in the live "Reunited" episode. The live grand finale included a reunion with all eliminated queens, with RuPaul revealing she had invited her husband to her hotel, a breach of contract, and officially crowned Sharon Needles as the winner. Ages, names, and cities stated are at the time of filming.
